description: Eight named garment tasks, with the original garment-only defaults preserved.
count_scope: Eight distinct task ids; five original garment-only selections retain their original start, instruction and evaluator. Four existing tasks additionally select the new contract explicitly. No random seeds or new train/test split.
split_note: No train/test split exists in this baseline; none invented.

evaluator.scope: Environment-owned task success; not physical qualification.

qualification: Defined task catalogue; does not imply every variation passed physical qualification.

task_set_v1.score_rule: 1 if success else 0.9 * continuous start-relative progress; crossings give zero. Shirt keeps its original evaluator.
task_set_v1.qualification: Code and constructed-state checks only; not yet run with the simulator or render-checked. Authored starts must pass existing IPC/table guards and bounded settling at runtime; failure to qualify aborts construction.

task_set.note: The render-checked eight: every untouched start rendered with success false and score 0. Differs from task_set_v1: tee/half_fold and towel/roll replace asymmetric/tie_untangle and jeans/leg_align_fold (on Linux the unchanged P13 reset loader rejects the asymmetric top and the jeans; both stay selectable under laundry-tasks-v2, outside the eight); every start settles before its zero point (at least 3 s, two steady 0.5 s blocks, at most 30 s); thirds_fold counts cloth crossings, so a correct letter fold passes; the ties are bunched on their free distal parts, crossing-free. The shirt keeps its original selection and evaluator.
task_set.score_rule: 1 if success else 0.9 * continuous start-relative progress; crossings give zero. Shirt keeps its original evaluator.
task_set.qualification: Constructed-state checks and render checks of the untouched starts (success false, score 0). Every start must pass the existing IPC/table guards (authored starts) and bounded settling at runtime; failure to qualify aborts construction.

swapped_out.why: garment does not construct on Linux with the unchanged reset loader (environment code)
